text: now simulate two epidemic models: SEIR, assumes exponential latent period SE4_4IR, uses fitted Erlang latent period structure generate trajectories two scenarios: intervention intervention
code: SEIR_ERLANG_ODE <- function(t, y, p) {      kE <- p$Esubstates   # Number of Erlang E substates   kI <- p$Isubstates   # Number of Erlang I substates      dydt <- numeric(kE + kI + 1)      # E1   dydt[1] <- (1 - p$eps) * (p$beta / p$N) * sum(y[(kE + 1):(kE + kI)]) * (p$N - sum(y)) - p$sigma * y[1]      # E2 to EkE   if (kE > 1) {     Ecount <- 1     while (Ecount < kE) {       dydt[Ecount + 1] <- p$sigma * y[Ecount] - p$sigma * y[Ecount + 1]       Ecount <- Ecount + 1     }   }      # I1   dydt[kE + 1] <- p$sigma * y[kE] - p$gamma * y[kE + 1]      # I2 to IkI   if (kI > 1) {     Icount <- 1     while (Icount < kI) {       dydt[Icount + 1 + kE] <- p$gamma * y[Icount + kE] - p$gamma * y[Icount + 1 + kE]       Icount <- Icount + 1     }   }      # Final recovered / removed compartment   dydt[kI + kE + 1] <- p$gamma * y[kI + kE]      list(dydt) }

code: # 1. Defining Population Parameters N <- 1e6 T <- 400 tspan <- 0:T  # 2. Define SEIR - Exponential Waiting Time Assumption Params Ro_1 <- 2.1 gamma <- 0.5 sigma <- OG_sigma beta_1 <- Ro_1 * gamma  # 3. Solve for SEIR - Exponential Waiting Time Assumption early exp growth rate r_eq <- c(1 / (gamma * sigma),           1 / gamma + 1 / sigma,           1 - Ro_1)  # R polyroot expects coefficients in increasing powers: # a0 + a1*x + a2*x^2 x <- polyroot(rev(r_eq)) r_1 <- max(Re(x[abs(Im(x)) < 1e-8]))  # 4. Using the prior K_star solve for SE4IR - Erlang Waiting Time Assumption # by equating the early exponential growth rate to what was calculated above nE <- K_star   # Obtained from GenErlangFit as number of substates for E nI <- 1  Ro_n <- (r_1 / gamma) * ((1 + r_1 / (sigma * nE))^nE) / (1 - (1 + r_1 / (gamma * nI))^(-nI)) beta_n <- Ro_n * gamma

what: 6.3 Running SEIR and SE4IR simulations without interventions
title: An Application of GenErlangFit to Epidemic Modeling
code: # Simulate K = 1 SEIR p1 <- list(   N = N,   beta = beta_1,   sigma = sigma,   gamma = gamma,   Esubstates = 1,   Isubstates = 1,   eps = 0 )  y0_1 <- c(E1 = 0, I1 = 1, R = 0)  SE1IR_noint <- ode(   y = y0_1,   times = tspan,   func = SEIR_ERLANG_ODE,   parms = p1 )  SE1IR_noint <- as.data.frame(SE1IR_noint)  SE1IR_noint$S <- N - rowSums(SE1IR_noint[, c("E1", "I1", "R")])   # Simulate K = nE SE4IR p4 <- list(   N = N,   beta = beta_n,   sigma = sigma * nE,   gamma = gamma,   Esubstates = nE,   Isubstates = nI,   eps = 0 )  y0_n <- c(rep(0, nE), 1, 0) names(y0_n) <- c(paste0("E", 1:nE), "I1", "R")  SE4IR_noint <- ode(   y = y0_n,   times = tspan,   func = SEIR_ERLANG_ODE,   parms = p4 )  SE4IR_noint <- as.data.frame(SE4IR_noint)  SE4IR_noint$S <- N - rowSums(SE4IR_noint[, c(paste0("E", 1:nE), "I1", "R")])

code: # 1. Set up intervention params intervention_day <- 45 beta_reduction <- 0.5  # 50% reduction  # Time spans tspan_before <- 0:intervention_day tspan_after <- intervention_day:T   # 2. Run for E = 1 # Before intervention SE1IR_before <- ode(   y = y0_1,   times = tspan_before,   func = SEIR_ERLANG_ODE,   parms = p1 )  SE1IR_before <- as.data.frame(SE1IR_before)  # After intervention p1_after <- p1 p1_after$beta <- beta_1 * beta_reduction  y0_1_after <- SE1IR_before[nrow(SE1IR_before), -1] y0_1_after <- as.numeric(y0_1_after) names(y0_1_after) <- names(y0_1)  SE1IR_after <- ode(   y = y0_1_after,   times = tspan_after,   func = SEIR_ERLANG_ODE,   parms = p1_after )  SE1IR_after <- as.data.frame(SE1IR_after)  # Combine SE1IR_int <- bind_rows(   SE1IR_before,   SE1IR_after[-1, ] )  # Add S SE1IR_int$S <- N - rowSums(SE1IR_int[, c("E1", "I1", "R")])   # 3. Run for E = 4 # Before intervention SE4IR_before <- ode(   y = y0_n,   times = tspan_before,   func = SEIR_ERLANG_ODE,   parms = p4 )  SE4IR_before <- as.data.frame(SE4IR_before)  # After intervention p4_after <- p4 p4_after$beta <- beta_n * beta_reduction  y0_4_after <- SE4IR_before[nrow(SE4IR_before), -1] y0_4_after <- as.numeric(y0_4_after) names(y0_4_after) <- names(y0_n)  SE4IR_after <- ode(   y = y0_4_after,   times = tspan_after,   func = SEIR_ERLANG_ODE,   parms = p4_after )  SE4IR_after <- as.data.frame(SE4IR_after)  # Combine SE4IR_int <- bind_rows(   SE4IR_before,   SE4IR_after[-1, ] )  # Add S SE4IR_int$S <- N - rowSums(SE4IR_int[, c(paste0("E", 1:nE), "I1", "R")]) # 1. Create Cumulative Infection Data Frames SE1IR_noint_cuminf <- SE1IR_noint %>%   transmute(time = time, cum_inf = (I1 + R) / N * 100)  SE4IR_noint_cuminf <- SE4IR_noint %>%   transmute(time = time, cum_inf = (I1 + R) / N * 100)  SE1IR_int_cuminf <- SE1IR_int %>%   transmute(time = time, cum_inf = (I1 + R) / N * 100)  SE4IR_int_cuminf <- SE4IR_int %>%   transmute(time = time, cum_inf = (I1 + R) / N * 100)   # 2. Create Daily Incidence Data Frames SE1IR_noint_Inc <- SE1IR_noint %>%   transmute(time = time, inc = c(0, diff(I1 + R)))  SE4IR_noint_Inc <- SE4IR_noint %>%   transmute(time = time, inc = c(0, diff(I1 + R)))  SE1IR_int_Inc <- SE1IR_int %>%   transmute(time = time, inc = c(0, diff(I1 + R)))  SE4IR_int_Inc <- SE4IR_int %>%   transmute(time = time, inc = c(0, diff(I1 + R)))

what: The Problem with Exponential Waiting Times
title: What is the Linear Chain Trick?
text: Compartmental models widely used epidemiology describe individuals move disease states—Susceptible (S), Exposed (E), Infectious (), Recovered (R). models typically formulated systems ordinary differential equations (ODEs) constant transition rates compartments. Despite widespread use, fundamental limitation models assumption constant transition rates compartments, implicitly imposes exponentially distributed waiting times within state. exponential distribution unique “memoryless” property: probability leaving compartment whether individual just arrived long time. results distribution many individuals short waiting times, others extremely long durations, relatively near mean. many biological processes, unrealistic. Incubation periods, infectious durations, recovery times often cluster around characteristic value rather exhibiting high variance exponential distribution.

title: What is the Linear Chain Trick?
text: Linear Chain Trick (LCT) technique constructing compartmental ODE models realistic waiting time distributions preserving linear ODE structure. exploits fact Erlang(K, λEr) distributed waiting time mathematically equivalent sum K independent exponential waiting times, rate λEr.Erlang probability density function given follows: f(x;K,λ)=λKxK−1e−λx(K−1)!,x≥0, f(x; K, \lambda) = \frac{\lambda^K x^{K-1} e^{-\lambda x}}{(K-1)!}, \qquad x \ge 0, allows single compartment partitioned K sub-compartments, sub-compartment retains exponentially distributed waiting times, keeping ODEs linear straightforward solve. two parameters (.e., number sub-compartments (K) transition rate (λEr)), Erlang distributions can approximate wide range shapes. K increases, distribution becomes peaked around mean, better capturing characteristic durations observed real disease processes enabling close fits many empirical distributions. principal advantage Erlang distribution ability modulate variability waiting times holding mean fixed, making particularly suitable processes exhibit less variance exponential distribution allows.

Allowing different rates compartments, entirely different compartmental structures, opens larger family phase-type distributions, including hypoexponential, hyper-Erlang, Coxian distributions (see Hurtado & Kirosingh 2019 details). tool supports one extension: Erlang-Exponential distributions, add one additional compartment different rate (λExp) K Erlang sub-compartments. three-parameter distribution can reproduce right-skewed empirical distributions compared standard Erlang distributions, providing additional flexibility fitting real-world data.

text: Kolmogorov-Smirnov Cramer-von Mises goodness--fit statistics (Erlang_Fit_v2_Pvalue ErlangFuncs.R; ErlangExp_Fit_v2_Pvalue ErlangExpFuncs.R) revised correctly implement standard closed-form definitions, following D’Agostino & Stephens (1986), Goodness--Fit Techniques. Independent unit tests validating statistics base R (ks.test) goftest package (cvm.test, ad.test) added test suite confirm correctness prevent regression. Removed non-ASCII characters (en dashes, curly apostrophes, accented characters, multiplication signs) source files roxygen documentation (ErlangFuncs.R, ErlangExpFuncs.R, MainDriver.R, DESCRIPTION), triggered R CMD check warning. Internal diagnostic plotting code used deprecated ggplot2 ..density.. syntax; updated after_stat(density).
